note: <show> is 4 alphanumeric characters. <studio-or-franchise> is an optional 2-char prefix used only where a collision with another studio's show code is a concern. Parts of the Show ID are joined by dashes because it is still one field.
<series> is 4 alphanumeric characters — 'got' is invalid because it is only three. Episode is a production sequence and may not match the airing sequence.

padding: portion-number zero-padded to a show-wide width
note: 2-4 alphanumeric characters. Avoid values that start with the reserved words unless they are the reserved designator. Sequences named with 'act' are act designators.
Unique within the sequence. '0000' is reserved for work where the concept of a shot does not apply — a model, or an effect spanning shots. Conventionally numbering starts at 0100.
A different instance number is a distinct plate, not a different version — EL01 fire, EL02 smoke.
Two alphanumeric characters assigned by the production VFX department. 'dd' Digital Domain, 'im' Industrial Light and Magic.

padding: 3 digits minimum; widen show-wide if >999 possible
note: Always the same number of numerals across a show. Revision 10 is 'v010' at three digits and 'v0010' at four.
Present only when a non-primary variant exists. The primary — best — version omits this field entirely.

padding: zero-pad numeric labels to a fixed width
note: Only when more than one camera shot simultaneously. 'l' and 'r' are the stereo pair; 'c' is centre.
Alphanumeric and dash only. Must stay constant for the life of the production — never 'doms-beard' one day and 'doms-facialhair' the next.
Which version of this specification the name was encoded against.
Preceded by a period rather than an underscore. Present for single-frame files (DPX, EXR); absent when the file holds all frames (MOV). By convention starts at 1001.
